did.unittitle: New Hampshire Coalition to Abolish the Death Penalty Records
did.abstract: This collection documents the day-to-day activities of the New Hampshire Coalition to Abolish the Death Penalty.
did.physloc: The materials are located onsite in the department.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: The New Hampshire Coalition to Abolish the Death Penalty was comprised of numerous organizations and individuals who were committed to ending the death penalty and preventing its expansion in the state of New Hampshire through outreach, advocacy, public demonstration, and education. Built on a community of citizen volunteers, religious groups, human rights activists, and relatives of murder victims, the Coalition would regularly bring experts on various death penalty issues to NH to share their experience with the public and the legislature. Through their advocacy efforts, the Coalition often meet with legislators, regularly attended legislative hearings, and supported the work of like-minded legislators to end the death penalty.

In May 2019, following the successful work of the Coalition and others, New Hampshire abolished the death penalty when the state Senate voted to override Gov. Chris Sununu's 2018 veto of a bill to repeal capital punishment. A week earlier the New Hampshire House also voted to override the veto.

Following the state's abolishment of capital punishment, the Coalition wound down from its multi-year efforts, but maintained a presence in the state to respond to any possible effort to reinstate the death penalty and to share its journey with other organizations fighting to abolish the death penalty in other states or countries.

scopecontent.head: Content Description
scopecontent.p: This collection contains legislative files, meeting minutes, correspondence, subject files, press releases, newspaper clippings, promotional materials, financial materials, and general day-to-day activities of the Coalitions members. It also includes press releases, conference materials, promotional materials, playbook guides, and other handouts from organizations and indivduals other than the Coalitian that shared similar goals or initiatives.

Researchers should note, however, that the collection does not contain materials from the Coalitian in the imediate events prior to, during, and imediatly after the final legislation to repeal capital punishment, Gov. Chris Sununu's veto, and the overide of said veto by both chambers of the General Court of New Hampshire.
